evals.prompt: I need to run claude in an automated CI pipeline with no interactive prompts. What flags should I use?
evals.expected_output: Recommends `--headless` mode for CI automation, mentions `--bare` for machine-readable output, notes that headless does single-turn execution with no interactive permission prompts, and provides the example `claude --headless -p "your prompt"`.

assertions.text: Mentions --headless flag as the primary mode for CI/automation
Mentions --bare flag as an alternative for machine-readable output
States headless mode runs single-turn execution
Notes that headless mode has no interactive permission prompts
Provides a command example with --headless and -p

evals.prompt: I want Claude to explore the codebase and then plan a feature. How do I spawn sub-agents?
evals.expected_output: Describes built-in sub-agents available in interactive sessions: @Explore for codebase exploration, @Plan for task planning, and @agent for general delegation. Notes that sub-agents run as child processes sharing the parent's context and permissions.

assertions.text: Mentions @Explore for codebase exploration
Mentions @Plan for task planning
Mentions @agent for general-purpose delegation
States sub-agents run as child processes within the CLI
Notes sub-agents share parent context and permissions
Indicates sub-agents require interactive session mode

evals.prompt: I need to continue a Claude session from earlier today. How do I resume it?
evals.expected_output: Describes --continue to resume the most recent session, --session <name> to resume a named session, and --session-name <name> to name the current session. Mentions --fork to duplicate session state and --no-persist for ephemeral work.

assertions.text: Mentions --continue flag to resume the most recent session
Mentions --session <name> to resume a named session
Mentions --session-name <name> to assign a name to the current session
Mentions --fork to duplicate session state
Mentions --no-persist for ephemeral tasks
States session data is stored locally and survives CLI restarts

evals.prompt: How do I get claude output in JSON format so I can parse it with jq in a script?
evals.expected_output: Describes --output json for structured JSON per turn and --output stream-json for one JSON object per line. Provides a jq example showing how to extract assistant content from stream-json output. Notes this is useful in CI pipelines.

assertions.text: Mentions --output json flag for structured JSON output
Mentions --output stream-json flag for streaming JSON
Provides a jq example with the pipe operator and select filter
Notes JSON output is useful in CI pipelines
States stream-json outputs one JSON object per line

evals.prompt: I want to cap Claude's spending in a session. How do I set a budget and turn limit?
evals.expected_output: Describes --max-budget-usd <amount> as a hard cap that terminates the session when reached, and --max-turns <n> to limit conversation turns. Mentions --model for cost control (e.g., haiku for simple queries, higher-effort models for complex tasks). Notes the CLI returns partial results when budget is reached.

assertions.text: Mentions --max-budget-usd flag as a hard spending cap
Mentions --max-turns flag to limit conversation turns
Mentions --model flag for selecting lower-cost models
States --max-budget-usd terminates the session when the threshold is reached
Notes the CLI returns partial results when budget is reached
Mentions model cost tradeoffs (haiku for simple, higher-effort for complex)
